safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any sensation of throat closing.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not document a denial of throat closing (only tingling is noted).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: If a true denial of throat closing sensation were omitted, the record may overstate airway involvement and prompt more aggressive triage/monitoring than necessary. This is more likely to lead to unnecessary escalation rather than missed anaphylaxis treatment.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no previous similar episodes.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention in the generated facts of no prior similar episodes.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting absence of prior similar episodes has limited impact on acute management of possible anaphylaxis, where current symptoms drive urgent treatment/EMS activation. It may reduce context for allergy risk counseling but is unlikely to change immediate care.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither Gold nor transcript clearly document denial of lip swelling; transcript indicates uncertainty ('not sure... can definitely feel something') rather than a denial.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting a denial of lip swelling when the patient was uncertain could falsely downplay evolving anaphylaxis/angioedema and reduce perceived urgency of airway risk. This can contribute to delayed escalation (e.g., epinephrine/ED evaluation) if future clinicians rely on the note.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold does not list regular/PRN antihistamines as a home medication; transcript only indicates the patient should be given/take an antihistamine now, not that it is an established PRN medication.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Listing antihistamines as a home PRN medication when it was only advised acutely can distort medication reconciliation and future clinical assumptions (e.g., that symptoms are already being treated). This typically causes low-level harm such as confusion, minor delays, or additional clarification.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Same as HPI denies lip swelling: not supported; transcript suggests uncertainty rather than denial.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: A false ROS denial of lip swelling can similarly misrepresent possible angioedema/anaphylaxis severity and may decrease clinician vigilance for airway compromise. In an allergic reaction context, this carries meaningful risk of delayed urgent treatment if trusted.
